_provenance.description: Final reported results for the VERDICT study. These are the figures cited in the dissertation and the README.
_provenance.run_environment: Google Colab, single free T4 GPU, 4-bit quantised local inference plus one free-tier API judge
_provenance.note: The per-run artefacts in datasets/processed/ are regenerated on every execution and reflect whatever panel was last active. This file is the pinned, citable summary. See results/README.md.

python_securityeval.metric_note: The benchmark contains only vulnerable samples, so precision is trivially 1.000 and ground-truth Cohen's kappa is degenerate. Recall is the discriminating metric; F1 is reported as the conventional summary.

exp_c_hybrid_best.note: Best configuration observed anywhere in the Python study.

exp_d_consensus.note: The pivotal negative result: consensus did not beat the best single judge.

exp_e_paired.note: The one task where consensus clearly beat static analysis, by a factor of three.

exp_f_adversarial.caveat: Robustness above 1.0 for PROMPT_INJECTION is an artefact of the 30-sample stratified subsample interacting with which samples were perturbed. It is not a real strengthening under attack and should be re-measured on the full benchmark.

plc_stmutants.design: differential mutant-vs-reference discrimination with identity controls
plc_stmutants.metric_note: The corpus is all-positive, so a raw detection rate rewards a response bias. Identity controls (reference compared against itself) must not be flagged; a model that flags them is penalised.

two_judge_rescore.note: Phi-2 is dropped because its 2048-token context cannot hold the two-version differential prompt, so it abstains on every pair. This tests the fair question: do the two working judges together beat the best single model?
two_judge_rescore.conclusion: No fusion of the two working judges reaches Mistral Nemo alone. The two are anti-correlated (Cohen's kappa = -0.12), and combining anti-correlated raters cannot beat the better one.

verification_confidence.note: Only 1 of 60 mutations escaped every detector, at the cost of routing 88% of cases to human review.

response_bias_incident.description: On the first PLC run, scored naively as single-snippet detection on the all-positive corpus, the smallest model appeared best and the largest appeared worst.
response_bias_incident.diagnosis: Qwen2.5-1.5B labelled essentially every input faulty, which is correct on every sample of an all-positive corpus. Its confidence was flat at 0.95 and it flagged 43% of identity controls as deviating.
response_bias_incident.resolution: The differential design with identity controls reversed the ranking. Do not cite the naive figures.

plc_stmutants.not_implemented: The symbolic-execution / runtime-monitoring arm of STMutants RQ-D requires an executable ST semantics (cf. K-ST, Wang et al. 2023) and is declared as future work rather than silently skipped.

cross_domain_findings: A single capable model beat every combination of the others in both domains, each time with inter-rater agreement no better than chance to explain why.

Evaluation design determined the conclusion: an all-positive benchmark inflated a weak model to a perfect score in both domains, and was only defused by an explicit negative signal (patched samples in Experiment E, identity controls in Experiment ST).

The contribution of static analysis flips sign between domains. It helped on Python security weaknesses and actively hurt on PLC functional mutations, so 'hybrid is best' is a statement about a domain rather than a general law.
